zh.summary: 用虛構教材中心的故事、誘因與進門情境，理解 Pretexting、Baiting、Tailgating，分清身分、授權、風險與證據。

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-04｜情境編造、誘餌與尾隨進入
Module 09：Social Engineering（社交工程） 本課核心：Pretexting、Baiting、Tailgating。建議分段閱讀 10～15 分鐘。
一、先說結論：合理的故事、吸引人的東西、已經打開的門，都不是授權
前一課 M09-03 談電話、簡訊與身分冒充，提醒我們「看起來像本人，不等於已驗證」。今天再往前一步：即使沒有假網站、沒有駭客程式，對方也可能讓我們替他跨過原本過不去的界線。
想像你在虛構的 Northstar 教材中心工作。辦公室有門禁，電腦裡有學員私人作答。某位來訪者說：「我是維修廠商，今天臨時來處理故障。」他拿著一支標示「課程免費工具」的隨身碟，並想趁同事刷卡後一起進辦公區。
先別急著認定他就是攻擊者；這是一個需要查證的合成情境。我們要拆開三種可能的操弄：

items: 理由：用一個故事，讓不尋常的要求看起來合理。
誘因：用你想要的東西，讓你願意採取某個動作。
通行：利用別人的開門機會，略過自己應完成的進入檢查。

sourceBody.text: 本課不是教你對所有人失去信任，而是把「願意幫忙」與「可以略過程序」分開。
二、先建立知識地圖：三種手法不是固定攻擊順序

visual.caption: 圖1：三個角度看同一個要求
visual.description: 理由、誘因與入口是分析視角；不是必然依序發生的步驟。

items.title: 理由、誘因、入口
items.body: Pretexting 用情境使要求合理；Baiting 用吸引力促使行動；Tailgating 利用別人的通行。三者可以分開或並存。

items.title: 共同判斷
items.body: 看對方要求的行動與跨越的權限界線。可信故事、好處或已開啟的門，都不能自動批准這次操作。

items.title: 連線語意
items.body: 虛線只表示概念關聯，沒有先後或因果承諾，不是一條固定攻擊流程。

sourceBody.text: 圖1圖說： 三個概念連到同一個判斷核心：「對方希望我替他做什麼？」圖中的概念連線不是實際資料傳輸，也不是一定先編故事、再放誘餌、最後進門的時間順序。

rows: Pretexting（情境編造／藉口詐術）
對方編了什麼理由，讓要求變得合理？
聲稱有緊急維修，要求略過原本的確認
Baiting（誘餌）
對方拿什麼吸引你做出某個動作？
用免費工具或好奇內容誘導使用未知檔案
Tailgating（尾隨進入）
誰想利用別人的通行，跨過實體管制邊界？
未獨立核驗的訪客跟在刷卡員工後面進入

sourceBody.text: 它們可以單獨出現，也可以在同一事件中結合。M09-02 分「鎖定誰」，M09-03 分「用什麼管道、冒充誰」，本課分「用什麼理由、誘因或通行方式」。這些是不同觀察角度，不是互斥標籤。
三、Pretexting：先造一個情境，讓你覺得這個要求說得通
Pretext 的意思是藉口或表面理由。Pretexting 是刻意捏造或操弄情境，讓接觸、索取資料或要求存取看起來合理。 加拿大資安中心的定義也把它描述為以虛構故事建立可信理由，誘導提供資訊或存取。[加拿大資安中心：Social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)
例如，對方不只是說「我是維修人員」，而是加上一套理由：「主管叫我趕快修，窗口正在開會，先讓我進去，之後再補登記。」
其中可以分兩層：

items: Impersonation（身分冒充）：我假扮成誰。
Pretexting（情境編造）：我用什麼故事，使這項要求看起來有必要。

sourceBody.text: 兩者常重疊，但不同。對方也可能不冒充某個特定名字，只虛構一個緊急情境。另一方面，真實維修也可能很急；我們不能只憑「急」就斷定詐騙。
### 真正該驗證的是「人＋事＋範圍」
假設公司確認來訪者確實是合作廠商，這也不代表他今天獲准進入所有房間、讀取所有資料。
Authentication（身分驗證） 是確認身分所需的條件；Authorization（授權） 是決定能做哪些事。這就是 M01-03 與 M09-03 已經出現的界線。
可以從既有可信窗口核對：

items: 1. 有沒有這次工作安排？
2. 來的人是不是指定人員？
3. 被核准進入哪個區域、處理哪些設備？
4. 是否需要接待、陪同及操作紀錄？

visual.caption: 圖2：獨立核實身分與工作範圍
visual.description: Pretexting｜可信的姓名、職稱或真實身分，都不能代替本次授權。

items.title: 收到請求
items.body: 先不執行提供資料或變更存取的要求；跨出可疑來源控制的聯絡資訊。

items.title: 獨立查證
items.body: 使用既有可信通訊錄或正式服務台，核實身分、請求真實性及本次對象、範圍和時限。

items.title: 兩條結果
items.body: 兩者都確認後，依最小必要範圍執行並留存紀錄；不符或不確定時停止，轉交適當窗口。箭頭是防禦決策流程，不是資料傳輸。

sourceBody.text: 圖2圖說： 箭頭表示本課的防守決策流程。身分確認與工作範圍確認是不同檢查；只有兩者符合既有程序，才進入有限度的執行。不明確時轉交正式窗口，不是自行猜測批准。
這裡的 Independent verification（獨立查證）延續上一課：用自己原先知道的服務台、承辦人或系統確認，不只打對方提供的號碼。澳洲資安指引也要求對要求改設定、執行程式或略過控制的行為進行獨立查證。[澳洲資安中心：社交工程指引](https://www.cyber.gov.au/guidance/learn-about-social-engineering)
四、Baiting：不是破解你的電腦，而是讓你先做出它需要的動作
Baiting 是用吸引人的承諾或物品，誘導對方採取會讓攻擊者受益的行動。 可能利用好奇、想省錢、想拿到工具或怕錯失機會等心理。
本課的「免費課程工具」隨身碟，就是可能的誘餌例子。但看到免費工具，不代表一定惡意；要看來源、要求及後續動作，不能單靠標籤定案。
它也不限於隨身碟。例如一個來路不明的「免費素材」入口，可能要求你輸入公司帳號，或安裝沒有核准的程式。誘餌不一定含惡意程式，也可能只是誘導交出資料。 官方資料同時列出惡意程式與資訊揭露等可能結果。[巴布亞紐幾內亞 NCSC：Social Engineering](https://www.ncsc.gov.pg/social-engineering/)
### 把「誘惑」和「後果」拆開
可以想成三個部分：

items: 表面利益：我以為能得到什麼？
被要求的動作：我需要先插入、開啟、登入、安裝或提供什麼？
可能影響：這個動作可能讓誰碰到我的裝置、帳號或資料？

sourceBody.text: 不是所有動作都會造成相同後果。插入未知裝置、開啟檔案、允許程式執行、輸入密碼，是不同事件；是否發生程式執行或資料存取，要依實際裝置、系統設定與證據確認。

visual.caption: 圖3：誘餌接觸與防守路徑
visual.description: Baiting｜免費檔案、獎品或陌生 USB：先辨識來源與處理邊界。

items.title: 未知不等於已證實惡意
items.body: 免費檔案或陌生 USB 有吸引力，不表示可信；不要在工作或家用裝置上插入、開啟來試。

items.title: 安全處理路線
items.body: 只回報發現地點及來源資訊，依正式窗口指示保全與交接；獲授權人員決定是否及如何分析。

items.title: 連線與風險
items.body: 綠箭頭表示通報與轉交流程，不是把 USB 插入另一部電腦。紅色叉號代表禁止路徑；紅色虛線代表條件式風險，不是已證實感染。

sourceBody.text: 圖3圖說： 未知來源在信任邊界外。正常處理箭頭通往核准的接收與檢查程序，不是直接連進日常工作電腦；圖中的虛線後果是可能風險，並非已證明發生。
### 遇到未知隨身碟，先不要替它找一台電腦試試
不要插入工作電腦，也不要帶回家用私人電腦測。依組織程序交給負責窗口；需要分析時，由具備授權、合適隔離環境與能力的人處理。
掃毒沒有告警，只能支持「該次檢查沒有偵測到它能辨識的問題」，不是無條件安全證明。這是一般證據判讀，不表示你現在需要自行做惡意程式分析。
組織可以搭配核准軟體來源、外接裝置使用政策、必要的裝置控制與最小權限。Least privilege（最小權限） 就是只給工作所需的存取與操作能力；它可以限制後果，但不能保證完全不出事。
五、Tailgating：門禁驗證了前面的人，不等於驗證了後面的人
Tailgating 在本課指未獲適當授權的人，跟著合法使用者穿過實體門禁或進入管制區。 它不是道路上的跟車，也不是本課在討論的網路連線劫持。
想像辦公區的門：員工刷卡成功，門開了；後方的人抱著箱子想一起進去。此時「門已打開」只是物理狀態，不能推論後方的人也已獲准。
佛羅里達大學的資安教材將跟隨進入、聲稱送貨、搬運大物品或忘記識別證，列為需留意的情境；這些外觀本身不是犯罪證據。[University of Florida：Tailgating](https://it.ufl.edu/security/learn-security/social-engineering/tailgating/)

visual.caption: 圖4：一人驗證不等於全隊通行
visual.description: Tailgating｜把「憑證獲准」與「實際進入的人」分開看。

items.title: 兩個人，各自核驗
items.body: 員工個人憑證與本次進入已獲准；訪客身分及權限尚未核對，不能直接沿用員工授權。

items.title: 邊界與路徑
items.body: 綠箭頭只表示員工本人可進入。訪客紅箭頭在門禁界線被阻止，轉往接待或門禁窗口依程序核對、登記與陪同。

items.title: 證據限制
items.body: 一筆有效刷卡紀錄，不等於進入人數或每個人的授權。這是空間教學圖，不要求讀者自行攔阻他人；安全及查驗依現場政策。

sourceBody.text: 圖4圖說： 左側是公共區，右側是管制區，中線是門禁邊界。員工通過自己的核驗；訪客的通行需要另一個核准流程。箭頭代表人的移動，沒有表示檔案已傳輸或系統已被駭。
### Tailgating 和 Piggybacking 要怎麼分？
你可能看過某些教材用「前面的人是否知情、是否幫忙」區分 Tailgating 與 Piggybacking（搭便車式進入）。不同來源用法不完全一致；例如 NCSC 直接將兩者並列，佛羅里達大學的 Tailgating 定義也包含誘使有權者放行。
因此，本課不把這種知情區分說成全球唯一標準。考題若給明確定義，就按題目語境判讀；實務上更重要的是：後方這個人是否完成必要核驗、誰有權放行、活動範圍有沒有被限制。
### 防守不是要你和可疑訪客起衝突
可依組織程序引導至接待窗口、核實訪客、登記與陪同；門禁設計也可考量逐人通行與異常告警。遇到不安全情況，以人身安全為先，交由保全或正式窗口處理，不自行攔阻、追逐或對抗。
「逐人核驗」也不等於每個場域一律用同一設備。機構仍需兼顧無障礙、緊急疏散、工作動線與合法政策；本課是風險模型，不是現場施工規格。
六、把三種手法放回同一個案例，但不混成一個結論
回到 Northstar：來訪者提出臨時維修理由、拿出免費工具、想跟著員工入內。我們可以問：

rows: 臨時維修並要求略過流程
可能的情境操弄
是否真的有工作安排與授權
免費工具要求先使用未知裝置
可能的誘餌
來源與要求是否可信、是否真的使用
跟在刷卡者後面進入
可能略過獨立門禁檢查
該訪客是否已有有效核准與陪同安排

sourceBody.text: 我們可以先暫停高風險動作、要求正式確認，不必先證明對方是壞人；但調查報告不能把所有可疑跡象直接寫成已確認攻擊。
這裡與先前 CEH 的連結是：

items: M09-01： 信任與善意不能取代驗證。
M09-02／03： 目標、管道、冒充角色與操弄手法可以同時標示。
M01-01： 進入辦公區可能影響資料機密性、設定完整性或服務可用性，但後果需要證據。
M01-02： 風險不只來自技術漏洞，也可能是訪客流程與權限安排的不足。
M01-03： 有合法測試授權才進行演練；本課只有桌上案例，不准自行測試陌生辦公室或把隨身碟放給別人撿。
M01-06／07： 人員、流程、門禁、裝置控制與紀錄形成縱深防禦；出事後依應變程序處理。

sourceBody.text: 七、證據觀念：記錄的是哪件事，就先只支持哪件事
一筆刷卡成功，不等於只有一人進門。 門禁紀錄通常是憑證與設備事件，不必然完整記下當時所有人的移動。要確認人數與身分，可能需要依法、依權限使用其他紀錄、接待資料及當事人說明。
同樣地：

items: 找到未知隨身碟，不代表有人插入。
有裝置連接紀錄，不代表所有檔案都已執行。
有程式執行紀錄，不代表已證明全部資料外洩。
有人進辦公區，不代表已登入受保護系統。

sourceBody.text: 這些是本課推理模型，不是某一套系統保證會產生的日誌欄位。Observation（觀察）、Inference（推論） 與 Verification（驗證） 要分開，跟 M01-02 一樣。
若已出現可疑操作，先透過正式管道通報，說清楚時間、地點、看到什麼、自己做過什麼。保留現有證據，不自行開啟未知檔案來確認，也不要任意刪除紀錄。
八、一個圖形推理小檢核
請看圖4，假設現在只有一筆員工刷卡成功紀錄。員工說有一名自稱維修人員的人跟著進門，對方留下一支標示免費工具的隨身碟；尚未查到工作安排、訪客核准、裝置連接與檔案執行紀錄。
請用自己的話回答同一個情境：

items: 1. 哪個箭頭或哪道檢查不能直接沿用員工的授權？為什麼「門開了」不等於訪客已獲准？
2. 維修理由、免費工具、跟隨進門，各可能對應哪個概念？現在能直接斷定全部是惡意攻擊嗎？
3. 你會先停止什麼、向哪個可信來源核實，以及補哪一類證據？

sourceBody.text: 不用長篇，也不必背名詞順序。參考答案另放預設收合區；公布答案不是本人作答，也不代表理解已通過。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：1. 哪道界線不能沿用員工的授權？
paragraphs: 訪客從公共區跨入管制區的那條路，不能因員工刷卡成功就自動成立。員工的憑證與存取權屬於員工；門打開只是設備狀態，沒有證明訪客身分、工作安排及可進入範圍都已核實。訪客也可能已有合法安排，所以要查訪客程序，而不是只憑外觀定罪。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：2. 三個概念與目前證據
paragraphs: 「臨時維修、先進去再說」若是捏造的合理化故事，可能是 Pretexting（情境編造）；用免費工具誘導使用未知裝置，可能是 Baiting（誘餌）；未經必要授權跟隨進門，可能是 Tailgating（尾隨進入）。這些分類可以同時成立。但目前缺少工作與訪客核准等紀錄，只能辨認風險與待查問題，不能逕稱全部惡意、程式已執行或資料已外洩。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：3. 先處置什麼，補什麼證據？
paragraphs: 先不使用未知隨身碟、不提供額外資料或存取，依程序聯絡既有接待／承辦／保全或資訊窗口，核對工作安排、訪客身分與範圍。人身安全優先，不自行攔阻或追逐。保存已有時間、地點與當事人陳述；若有權且必要，再交叉查訪客登記、門禁及相關影像、裝置連接與執行紀錄。這些紀錄可能不存在或不完整，應標示未知，不把缺紀錄當成沒發生，也不擅自製造新的危險測試。
推理重點：先辨認跨越的邊界，提出能驗證該邊界的證據，再依已知風險處置。不是多猜幾個攻擊名詞就比較正確。

sourceBody.text: 九、本課記住三句話

items: 1. Pretexting：理由看似合理，仍要核實人、事與授權範圍。
2. Baiting：先看被要求的動作，不要讓好奇或獎勵替你批准風險。
3. Tailgating：別人的驗證，不會自動變成你的通行權。

sourceBody.text: 下一個單元是 M09-05「Insider Threats & Identity Theft（內部威脅與身分竊用）」。本課的防守核心不是變得不友善，而是讓幫忙有安全、可驗證的做法。

en.summary: Use a fictional learning center to distinguish pretexting, baiting, and tailgating, with independent verification, authorization boundaries, and evidence limits.

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-04 | Pretexting, Baiting, and Tailgating
Module 09: Social Engineering Read in sections; allow about 10–15 minutes.
1. The main idea: a plausible story, an attractive offer, and an open door are not authorization

M09-03 covered voice calls, text messages, and impersonation. Something that looks authentic is not necessarily verified. Today we take that idea further: an adversary may persuade someone to cross a boundary for them without using a fake website or an exploit.

Imagine working at the fictional Northstar learning center. Its office has controlled entry, and its computers contain private learner responses. A visitor says they are an urgently dispatched maintenance contractor. They carry a USB drive labeled “free course tools” and try to enter with an employee who has just used their badge.
Do not immediately conclude that the visitor is an attacker. This is a synthetic situation requiring verification. Separate three possible mechanisms:

items: A reason: a story makes an unusual request seem reasonable.
An incentive: something desirable encourages a particular action.
Entry: someone uses another person's passage to skip their own access check.

sourceBody.text: The lesson is not to distrust everybody. It is to distinguish being helpful from skipping required procedures.
2. A knowledge map: three techniques, not a fixed attack sequence

visual.caption: Figure 1: Three ways to examine a request
visual.description: Reason, reward, and entry are lenses—not a required sequence.

items.title: Reason, incentive, entry
items.body: Pretexting supplies a plausible story; baiting supplies an incentive; tailgating uses another person’s passage. They may occur separately or together.

items.title: Shared decision
items.body: Examine the requested action and the authority boundary. A convincing story, desirable offer, or open door does not authorize this action.

items.title: Relationship meaning
items.body: Dotted lines show conceptual associations, not time order, causation, or a mandatory attack sequence.

sourceBody.text: Figure 1 caption: The concepts connect to one central question: what action does the requester want me to perform? Concept links are not data transfers or a claim that every incident proceeds from a story, to bait, to physical entry.

rows: Pretexting
What invented reason makes the request seem justified?
Claimed urgent maintenance used to bypass normal checks
Baiting
What desirable offer encourages an action?
A free tool or interesting content used to entice use of an unknown file
Tailgating
Who is using another person's passage to cross a physical boundary?
An unverified visitor entering behind a badged employee

sourceBody.text: These techniques can occur separately or together. M09-02 classified targets. M09-03 examined channels and claimed identities. This lesson examines reasons, incentives, and physical entry. These are different perspectives, not mutually exclusive labels.
3. Pretexting: build a story that makes the request seem necessary

A pretext is an apparent justification. Pretexting uses a fabricated or manipulated situation to make contact, a request for information, or an access request seem reasonable. The Canadian Cyber Centre likewise describes a false narrative used to build trust and seek information or access. [Canadian Cyber Centre: Social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)
The visitor might do more than claim to be a contractor. They add a justification: the manager wants the repair immediately, the contact is in a meeting, and registration can be completed later.
Separate two layers:

items: Impersonation: who am I pretending to be?
Pretexting: what story makes this request seem warranted?

sourceBody.text: They often overlap, but they are not identical. A person may invent an emergency without claiming a specific name. Real maintenance may also be urgent; urgency alone does not prove deception.
### Verify the person, the work, and its scope
Even if the company confirms that a visitor works for a real contractor, that does not authorize entry to every room or access to every file today.
Authentication checks the conditions needed to establish an identity. Authorization determines permitted actions. This is the same boundary introduced in M01-03 and M09-03.
Use an established trusted contact to check:

items: 1. Is this work actually scheduled or approved?
2. Is this the designated person?
3. Which areas and equipment are included?
4. Are reception, escort, and activity records required?

visual.caption: Figure 2: Verify identity and work scope independently
visual.description: Pretexting: a credible name, role, or real identity is not enough.

items.title: Receive a request
items.body: Do not immediately disclose information or change access. Leave contact information controlled by the suspicious source.

items.title: Independent verification
items.body: Use an established trusted directory or official service desk. Verify identity, request authenticity, and authorization for this object, scope, and time.

items.title: Two outcomes
items.body: If verified and authorized, perform only the necessary approved action and retain records. If inconsistent or uncertain, stop and refer. Arrows depict a defensive decision process, not data transfer.

sourceBody.text: Figure 2 caption: Arrows show a defensive decision process. Identity and work scope are separate checks. Limited execution follows only when the required checks satisfy the established procedure. Uncertainty goes to the authorized contact, not to an improvised approval.

Independent verification means using your established help desk, responsible contact, or system rather than relying only on contact details supplied by the requester. Australian guidance likewise calls for independent verification of requests to run code, change settings, or bypass controls. [Australian Cyber Security Centre guidance](https://www.cyber.gov.au/guidance/learn-about-social-engineering)
4. Baiting: persuade someone to perform the enabling action
Baiting uses an attractive promise or object to induce an action that benefits the adversary. It may appeal to curiosity, saving money, obtaining a tool, or fear of missing out.

The “free course tools” USB drive is a possible bait example. A free offer is not automatically malicious. Examine the source, the requested action, and what follows rather than deciding from a label alone.

Bait is not limited to USB drives. An unfamiliar “free assets” site might ask for a work account or an unapproved software installation. Baiting does not require malware: it may instead induce disclosure of information. Government guidance includes both malware installation and information disclosure as possible outcomes. [Papua New Guinea NCSC: Social Engineering](https://www.ncsc.gov.pg/social-engineering/)
### Separate the attraction from the consequence
Ask three questions:

items: What benefit do I expect to receive?
What must I first connect, open, install, enter, or disclose?
Who might gain access to my device, account, or information through that action?

sourceBody.text: Different actions do not imply identical outcomes. Connecting a device, opening a file, allowing execution, and entering a password are separate events. Whether execution or access actually occurred depends on the device, system configuration, and evidence.

visual.caption: Figure 3: Bait exposure and the safe handling path
visual.description: Baiting: a free file, prize, or unknown USB demands a source and handling check.

items.title: Unknown is not proven malicious
items.body: An attractive free file or unfamiliar USB drive is not automatically trusted. Do not connect or open it on work or home devices as a test.

items.title: Safe response route
items.body: Report discovery and source information to the official contact, preserve and hand over as directed. Authorized specialists decide whether and how to analyze it.

items.title: Connections and risk
items.body: Green arrows mean reporting and referral, not plugging the USB into another computer. The red cross blocks an unsafe route; red dotted lines depict conditional risk, not established infection.

sourceBody.text: Figure 3 caption: An unknown source begins outside the trust boundary. The safe handling arrow leads to an approved intake and examination process, not straight to a daily-use computer. Dashed consequences are potential risks, not established events.
### Do not find an ordinary computer to “try” an unknown USB drive

Do not connect it to a work computer or take it home to test on a personal computer. Follow the organization's intake procedure. If analysis is needed, authorized people with appropriate expertise and an appropriately isolated environment should handle it.

A scan with no alert means the particular check did not detect a problem it could recognize. It is not an unconditional safety guarantee. This is an evidence principle, not a request to perform malware analysis.

Organizations can combine approved software sources, removable-device policies, appropriate device controls, and least privilege: granting only the access and capabilities required for the job. Least privilege can limit consequences, but does not guarantee that no incident can occur.
5. Tailgating: checking the person in front does not check the person behind
In this lesson, tailgating is unauthorized entry through a physical access boundary by following a legitimate user. This is not road traffic behavior or a synonym for network session hijacking here.
An employee's badge succeeds and the office door opens. A person carrying boxes wants to enter behind them. The open door is a physical state, not proof that the second person is authorized.

The University of Florida lists following someone, claiming a delivery, carrying large items, and claiming a forgotten badge among situations to examine. These appearances alone are not proof of criminal intent. [University of Florida: Tailgating](https://it.ufl.edu/security/learn-security/social-engineering/tailgating/)

visual.caption: Figure 4: One verified entrant does not authorize the whole group
visual.description: Tailgating: distinguish an authorized credential from the people entering.

items.title: Two people, separate checks
items.body: The employee’s credential and entry are approved. The visitor’s identity and authorization remain unchecked; the visitor cannot inherit the employee’s permission.

items.title: Boundary and paths
items.body: The green arrow permits only the employee to enter. The visitor’s red route stops at the access boundary and refers to reception or access staff for verification, registration, and escort under policy.

items.title: Evidence limits
items.body: One valid badge event does not establish headcount or everyone’s permission. This is a teaching model, not an instruction to confront people; physical safety and checks follow site policy.

sourceBody.text: Figure 4 caption: The public area is on the left and the controlled area on the right, separated by an entry boundary. The employee passes their own check. The visitor requires a separate approved process. Arrows indicate people's movement, not file transfer or a confirmed system compromise.
### Tailgating and piggybacking

Some training materials distinguish tailgating from piggybacking according to whether the authorized person knows about or helps the entry. Terminology is not consistent across sources. The PNG NCSC lists them together, while the University of Florida's tailgating definition includes persuading authorized people to let someone in.

Do not treat the awareness distinction as a universal standard. If a question defines its terms, use that context. Operationally, ask whether the second person completed the required checks, who may authorize passage, and how their scope is limited.
### Protect the boundary without creating a confrontation

Use the organization's reception, visitor verification, registration, and escort procedure. Entry design may also include individual passage controls and alerts. If the situation feels unsafe, prioritize personal safety and contact security or the designated team. Do not physically block, chase, or confront someone yourself.

Individual verification does not mean every site needs the same equipment. Accessibility, emergency evacuation, work patterns, and applicable policies still matter. This lesson is a risk model, not a construction specification.
6. Put the techniques together without collapsing the evidence
Return to Northstar: the visitor gives an urgent maintenance reason, offers free tools, and wants to enter with an employee.

rows: Urgent maintenance and a request to bypass procedure
Possible use of a fabricated justification
Whether the work and access are actually authorized
Free tools requiring use of an unknown device
Possible bait
The source, requested action, and whether it was used
Entry behind a badged person
Possible bypass of an independent entry check
Whether the visitor already had valid approval and escort arrangements

sourceBody.text: You can pause a high-risk action and seek formal confirmation without first proving that the person is malicious. But an investigation must not turn every suspicious sign into a confirmed attack.
Connections to previous lessons:

items: M09-01: trust and helpfulness do not replace verification.
M09-02/03: target, channel, claimed identity, and manipulation technique can all be described together.
M01-01: entry may affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability; actual consequences require evidence.
M01-02: risks can arise from visitor processes and permission design, not only software flaws.
M01-03: real exercises require authorization. This is a tabletop lesson, not permission to test an unfamiliar office or leave USB drives for others to find.
M01-06/07: people, procedures, entry controls, device controls, and records form defense in depth; incidents follow the response process.

sourceBody.text: 7. Evidence: a record first supports the event it actually describes

One successful badge event does not prove that only one person entered. Access records usually describe credential and device events; they do not necessarily capture every person's movement. Confirming people and identity may require other lawfully and appropriately accessed records, reception information, and statements.
Likewise:

items: Finding an unknown USB drive does not prove anyone connected it.
A device-connection event does not prove every file executed.
An execution event does not prove all data was exfiltrated.
Physical office entry does not prove a protected-system login.

sourceBody.text: These are reasoning examples, not a claim that every product records the same fields. Keep observation, inference, and verification separate, as in M01-02.

Report suspicious activity through the established channel. Describe time, place, observations, and your actual actions. Preserve existing evidence. Do not open an unknown file to confirm a suspicion or arbitrarily erase records.
8. One visual reasoning check

Look at Figure 4. There is one successful employee badge event. The employee reports that a self-described maintenance visitor entered behind them and left a USB drive labeled “free tools.” Work approval, visitor authorization, device-connection records, and file-execution records have not yet been checked.
Use your own words to answer this single scenario:

items: 1. Which movement or check cannot inherit the employee's authorization? Why does an open door not prove visitor authorization?
2. Which concepts might describe the maintenance story, free tools, and entry behind the employee? Can all of them already be labeled malicious?
3. What would you stop first, which trusted source would you consult, and what evidence would you seek?

sourceBody.text: A short answer is enough. Reference answers belong in a separate initially collapsed section. Publishing an answer is not the learner's response or evidence of mastery.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 1. Which boundary cannot inherit the employee's authorization?
paragraphs: The visitor's path from the public area into the controlled area does not automatically become valid when the employee's badge succeeds. The employee's credential and rights belong to that employee. An open door is a device state, not proof of the visitor's identity, work approval, or permitted scope. A visitor might already have a legitimate arrangement, so check the process rather than judging from appearance.

An invented urgent-maintenance justification may be pretexting. Free tools used to induce use of an unknown device may be baiting. Entry behind an authorized person without required authorization may be tailgating. They may coexist. However, missing work and visitor-approval evidence means there are risks to investigate, not enough evidence to declare every action malicious, code execution established, or data exfiltrated.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 3. What to stop and what to verify
paragraphs: Do not use the unknown USB drive or provide additional information or access. Follow the established reception, responsible-contact, security, or IT process to verify work, identity, and scope. Prioritize personal safety; do not block or chase the person yourself. Preserve existing times, locations, and statements. Where authorized and necessary, correlate visitor records, access events and relevant video, device connections, and execution records. Those records may be absent or incomplete. Mark uncertainty instead of treating missing records as proof of no event or creating a new hazardous test.
Reasoning goal: identify the crossed boundary, seek evidence that can verify it, and act on the known risk. Guessing more attack labels is not a substitute.

sourceBody.text: 9. Three lines to remember

items: 1. Pretexting: a plausible reason still needs verified identity, work, and scope.
2. Baiting: examine the requested action; curiosity or a reward must not authorize risk.
3. Tailgating: another person's verification does not become your access right.

sourceBody.text: The next unit is M09-05, Insider Threats & Identity Theft. The aim is not to become unhelpful. It is to make helpful action safe and verifiable.
